slides.title: Professional Behaviour Applies Everywhere
slides.content: The same standards apply: In college. On placement. In employment. Professional behaviour includes: Being on time. Being prepared. Communicating early about problems. Treating people respectfully. Taking responsibility for mistakes and fixing them.

slides.title: Professionalism Is About Habits
slides.content: Professionalism is not something you switch on for interviews. It is demonstrated through: Reliability. Communication. Respect. Consistency. Accountability. These habits influence how others see you.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Professionalism Is About Habits'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Professionalism Is About Habits.

slides.title: Your Reference Starts Now
slides.content: Staff references are built from: Attendance. Punctuality. Reliability. Professional conduct. References focus on patterns over time, not isolated mistakes.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Your Reference Starts Now'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Your Reference Starts Now.

slides.title: Human Skills Matter
slides.content: Employers often hire based on more than qualifications. Key employability skills include: Explaining work clearly. Working effectively with others. Doing what you promised to do. Finding solutions independently. Handling change well. Taking action without being asked.

slides.title: Skills Assessment Results
slides.content: The Skills Assessment helps identify: Strengths. Development areas. Priorities for improvement. You should: Review your results carefully. Compare them with how others see you. Choose areas to develop.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Skills Assessment Results'? Select all that apply.

slides.title: Claims Need Evidence
slides.content: Weak statement: "I'm a good team player." Strong statement: "I organised project deadlines for my group and helped the team submit on time." The strongest applications include evidence rather than claims.

slides.content: What happened? What did you actually do? What does it demonstrate? Evidence can come from: College projects. Placements. Part-time jobs. Sports. Caring responsibilities. Volunteering.

slides.content: Navigate should contain: Skills assessment results. Strength statements. Digital CV information. Development plans. This information will support later applications and placements.
